es.summary: Disminución del flujo sanguíneo a los tejidos periféricos por enfermedad arterial o venosa, que produce dolor y riesgo de ulceración.
key_points: La aterosclerosis es la causa principal de la insuficiencia arterial.
La insuficiencia venosa se caracteriza por edema y cambios cutáneos.
El dolor claudicante indica isquemia muscular.
Complicaciones graves incluyen úlceras, gangrena y amputación.

pathophysiology: Acumulación de placa aterosclerótica reduce el calibre arterial.
Obstrucción venosa aumenta la presión capilar y causa edema.
Disminución del flujo provoca hipoxia tisular y daño celular.
signs_symptoms: Dolor al caminar que desaparece en reposo (claudicación).
Cambios de color: palidez, cianosis o rubor.
Edema, edema dependiente y edema con fóvea en insuficiencia venosa.
diagnostics: Ecografía Doppler muestra flujo reducido o reflujo venoso.
Angiografía por TC o resonancia para evaluar la anatomía.
Laboratorio: glucosa >126 mg/dL, colesterol LDL >130 mg/dL.
treatment: Ejercicio supervisado y control de factores de riesgo.
complications: Úlceras crónicas en pie o pierna.
nursing_care: Evaluar pulsos, tiempo de llenado capilar y color de piel cada turno.
Inspeccionar y registrar edema, úlceras o cambios cutáneos.
Controlar dolor y proporcionar analgesia según orden.
Mantener extremidades elevadas 15‑30 min, 3‑4 veces al día.
Aplicar medias de compresión según prescripción.
Promover marcha ambulatoria y ejercicios de rango de movimiento.
patient_teaching: Dejar de fumar y evitar exposición al humo.
Realizar caminatas diarias de 30‑45 min, según tolerancia.
Cuidar los pies: inspección diaria, mantener uñas cortas y piel hidratada.
Usar medias de compresión correctamente y cambiarlas según indicaciones.
Adherir al tratamiento farmacológico y controlar colesterol y glucosa.
Mantener dieta baja en grasas saturadas y rica en fibra.

outcomes: Mejora de la perfusión periférica: pulsos palpables en 48 h.
Reducción del dolor al caminar a <2 min en 1 semana.

interventions.action: Evaluar pulsos, tiempo de llenado capilar y color de piel cada turno.
interventions.rationale: Detectar cambios tempranos en la perfusión y guiar intervenciones.

interventions.action: Promover marcha ambulatoria progresiva según tolerancia.
interventions.rationale: Mejora la circulación colateral y reduce la claudicación.

interventions.action: Aplicar compresión graduada en caso de insuficiencia venosa.
interventions.rationale: Disminuye la presión venosa y previene edema.

interventions.action: Administrar antiplaquetario y estatina según prescripción.
interventions.rationale: Previene progresión de la aterosclerosis y eventos trombóticos.

interventions.action: Enseñar al paciente técnicas de cuidado de pies y auto‑inspección diaria.
interventions.rationale: Previene ulceraciones y complicaciones infecciosas.

outcomes: Mantener integridad cutánea sin aparición de úlceras en 30 días.
Piel intacta y sin signos de irritación al final del periodo de hospitalización.

interventions.action: Repositionar al paciente cada 2 horas, alternando posición supina y lateral.
interventions.rationale: Reduce la presión prolongada sobre áreas vulnerables.

interventions.action: Mantener la piel limpia y seca; usar humectantes si está seca.
interventions.rationale: Preserva la barrera cutánea y previene maceración.

interventions.action: Utilizar colchón o almohadilla anti‑úlceras según indicación.
interventions.rationale: Distribuye la presión y disminuye riesgo de daño tisular.

interventions.action: Evaluar y documentar la integridad cutánea diariamente.
interventions.rationale: Detecta precozmente cambios que requieran intervención.

interventions.action: Fomentar la movilidad activa o pasiva según tolerancia.
interventions.rationale: Mejora la perfusión y reduce la estasis venosa.

en.summary: Reduced blood flow to peripheral tissues due to arterial or venous disease, causing pain and risk of ulceration.
key_points: Atherosclerosis is the main cause of arterial insufficiency.
Venous insufficiency is characterized by edema and skin changes.
Severe complications include ulcers, gangrene, and amputation.

pathophysiology: Accumulation of atherosclerotic plaque narrows arterial lumen.
Venous obstruction increases capillary pressure and causes edema.
Reduced flow leads to tissue hypoxia and cellular damage.
signs_symptoms: Pain when walking that resolves at rest (claudication).
Color changes: pallor, cyanosis, or erythema.
Edema, dependent edema, and pitting edema in venous insufficiency.
diagnostics: Doppler ultrasound shows reduced flow or venous reflux.
CT or MRI angiography to assess anatomy.
treatment: Supervised exercise and risk factor control.
nursing_care: Assess pulses, capillary refill time, and skin color each shift.
Inspect and document edema, ulcers, or skin changes.
Monitor pain and provide analgesia as ordered.
Keep extremities elevated 15‑30 min, 3‑4 times daily.
patient_teaching: Quit smoking and avoid smoke exposure.
Take daily walks 30‑45 min as tolerated.
Care for feet: daily inspection, keep nails trimmed and skin moisturized.
Use compression stockings correctly and change as directed.
Adhere to medication regimen and monitor cholesterol and glucose.

outcomes: Improved peripheral perfusion: palpable pulses within 48 h.
Reduced walking pain to <2 min within 1 week.

interventions.action: Assess pulses, capillary refill time, and skin color each shift.
interventions.rationale: Detect early perfusion changes and guide interventions.

interventions.action: Promote progressive ambulation as tolerated.
interventions.rationale: Improves collateral circulation and reduces claudication.

interventions.action: Apply graduated compression if venous insufficiency present.
interventions.rationale: Reduces venous pressure and prevents edema.

interventions.action: Administer antiplatelet and statin as prescribed.
interventions.rationale: Prevents atherosclerosis progression and thrombotic events.

interventions.action: Teach patient foot care and daily self‑inspection techniques.
interventions.rationale: Prevents ulceration and infectious complications.

outcomes: Maintain skin integrity without ulcer development for 30 days.
Intact skin with no signs of irritation at end of hospitalization.

interventions.action: Reposition patient every 2 hours, alternating supine and lateral positions.
interventions.rationale: Reduces prolonged pressure on vulnerable areas.

interventions.action: Keep skin clean and dry; use emollients if dry.
interventions.rationale: Preserves skin barrier and prevents maceration.

interventions.action: Use pressure‑relieving mattress or pad as indicated.
interventions.rationale: Distributes pressure and lowers tissue injury risk.

interventions.action: Assess and document skin integrity daily.
interventions.rationale: Detects early changes requiring intervention.

interventions.action: Encourage active or passive mobility as tolerated.
interventions.rationale: Improves perfusion and reduces venous stasis.

sources.name: Clinical Nursing Skills: Peripheral Vascular System

key_points.1.quote: venous insufficiency will have pain that is described as dull and achy, lower leg edema, and sores located on the ankles.

key_points.2.quote: A primary symptom of peripheral vascular disease is intermittent claudication , a cramp-like muscle pain, burning sensation, or extreme fatigue in the calf, thigh, or buttocks that is induced by exercise and relieved by rest.

sections.pathophysiology.0.quote: Both peripheral artery disease (PAD) and peripheral vascular disease (PVD) involve narrowing of the peripheral blood vessels typically caused by a buildup of plaque.

sections.pathophysiology.1.quote: Blood flow to the legs becomes congested because of increased hydrostatic pressure caused by decreased function.

sections.pathophysiology.2.quote: When perfusion is altered or impaired, there is risk for issues to occur such as hypoxia, tissue damage, necrosis, and even shock.

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: But some of the more common risk factors include: Age - your risk of some diseases goes up as you get older Conditions that can affect the heart and blood vessels, such as diabetes or high cholesterol Family history of vascular or heart diseases Infection or injury that damages your veins Lack of exercise Obesity Pregnancy Sitting or standing still for long periods of time Smoking What are the symptoms of vascular diseases? sections.risk_factors.2.quote: Heart failure, hypertension, and deep vein thrombosis (DVT) are all disorders that must be accurately diagnosed to properly treat and alleviate edema.

sections.risk_factors.4.quote: But some of the more common risk factors include: Age - your risk of some diseases goes up as you get older Conditions that can affect the heart and blood vessels, such as diabetes or high cholesterol Family history of vascular or heart diseases Infection or injury that damages your veins Lack of exercise Obesity Pregnancy Sitting or standing still for long period

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: Intermittent claudication is pain in the calves, thighs, and buttocks that occurs when walking distances and is relieved with rest.

sections.signs_symptoms.1.quote: On assessment, the affected limb may feel cold to touch, pulses may be weak, and the skin will exhibit color changes such as pallor or decreased capillary refill due to insufficient blood getting to the limbs from arterial insufficiency.

sections.signs_symptoms.3.quote: An early indicator of venous dysfunction is dependent edema, which is measured by placing slight pressure with a finger in the area of swelling to determine the degree of pitting.

sections.treatment.0.quote: Medical therapies include pharmaceuticals, including statins and antiplatelet/anticoagulation agents, hypertension management if present, diabetes management if present, exercise, and smoking cessation as necessary.

sections.complications.2.quote: Disorders affecting this system can range from peripheral artery disease (PAD) and venous insufficiency to deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and varicose veins .

sections.complications.4.quote: Acute or critical limb ischemia may occur if left untreated.

sections.nursing_care.2.quote: Other interventions may include observing for deep vein thrombosis (DVT) , assessing popliteal and pedal pulses, assisting with position changes, and administering anticoagulants and pain medication as ordered.

sections.nursing_care.5.quote: Nurses also should provide patient and family education to include instructions on how to safely apply warmth to the area, encourage range-of-motion (ROM) exercises, exercise therapy, and ambulation as tolerated.

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: Patients are encouraged to avoid high-cholesterol foods and stop smoking to prevent further vasoconstriction.
